an instance of the template “Judgment and a remnant spared” — It rests on the text's own explanation. Corruption: "sin entered the world through one man, and death through sin, so also death was passed on to all men, because all sinned" (Rom 5:12) -- Genesis 3 and all who came after, in one verse; "There is no one righteous, not even one" (3:10) quotes Psalm 14, whose "corrupt" in 14:1 is the flood's verb, with God looking to see it as in Gen 6:12; "all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God" (3:23). Judgment: "the day of wrath, when God's righteous judgment will be revealed" (Rom 2:5), and on the cross, "My God, My God, why have You forsaken Me?" (Matt 27:46). Set apart: "I want those You have given Me to be with Me where I am" (John 17:24). Remnant: "everyone who believes in Him shall not perish" (John 3:16), sent to "make disciples of all nations" (Matt 28:19). New beginning: "He has risen" (Matt 28:6), and "if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation. The old has passed away. Behold, the new has come!" (2 Cor 5:17). The text itself ties this story to the flood's: Peter sets the eight saved in the ark beside "the resurrection of Jesus Christ" (1 Pet 3:20–21), and Jesus takes "I will strike the Shepherd" to himself (Matt 26:31), where Zechariah goes on, "a third will be left" (Zech 13:7–8).
